promptLatex: A sphere has radius $6$. What is the surface area of the sphere, in terms of $\pi$?
hintLatex: The surface area of a sphere is four times the area of its great circle.
The great circle has the same radius as the sphere, namely $6$.
solutionLatex:
The surface area of a sphere is $4 \pi r^{2}$, which is four times the area $\pi r^{2}$ of the great circle cut out by any plane through the centre.

With $r = 6$, the great circle has area $\pi \cdot 36 = 36\pi$, so the sphere has surface area $4 \cdot 36\pi = 144\pi$.

The volume of the same sphere is $\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} = 288\pi$, which is the number most often confused with this one.
